body:
/kind feature

**Gaps Identified With Kserve's Handling of the Knative Autoscaler Configuration** 
Currently, Kserve does not take into account the knative autoscaler configuration when creating knative services for Inference Services or Inference Graphs. This leads to several gaps in the way kserve handles the creation of knative services:

1. kserve does not account for the global knative configuration of `initial-scale`. This can lead to scenarios where the number of replicas created to initialize a knative revision does not fall into the range of the requested min or max replicas for the Inference Service or Inference Graph. Consider the following scenarios:

    1. knative is globally configured with an `initial-scale` value that exceeds the max replicas requested for an Inference Service or Inference Graph. In this scenario, the knative revision created will be initialized with a greater number of replicas created than what the user requested as the maximum value.
    2. knative is globally configured with an `initial-scale` value that exceeds the min replicas requested for an Inference Service, but is less than the requested max replicas. knative will always choose the larger of `min-scale` and `initial-scale` as the initial target scale for a knative revision. So, in this scenario the knative revision created will be initialized with a greater number of replicas created than the user requested minimum value. A prominent case of this scenario would be when the min replicas requested is 0. The default `initial-scale` value used by knative is 1, so if a user installs knative and kserve out of the box, there will always be 1 replica created to initialize the revision when min replicas 0 is requested.

2. kserve only [adds](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/pkg/controller/v1beta1/inferenceservice/reconcilers/knative/ksvc_reconciler.go#L92) the knative `autoscaling.knative.dev/max-scale` annotation to a knative service's template spec if the max replicas value requested for an Inference Service is a non zero value (**kserve never adds this annotation for Inference Graphs**). Due to this, if an Inference Service is requested with 0 max replicas, knative will use the globally configured `max-scale` value for the created knative revision, alternatively for Inference Graphs, the globally configured `max-scale` value will **always** be used. This presents a bug for the following scenario:

    1. knative is globally configured with a `max-scale-limit` value of 0, i.e. infinite scaling is allowed, and a `max-scale` value that is greater than 0. If a user desires to allow a requested Inference Service or Inference Graph to scale up infiinitely by requesting for the max replicas to be 0, this would not be possible since no `autoscaling.knative.dev/max-scale`  annotation is added, knative will fall back to using the global configuration which has a `max-scale` value that is greater than 0, effectively placing a limit on the scale.


**Proposed Solutions**
The scenarios mentioned in [1] above, while still leading to a confusing user experience, can be argued as the proper behavior a defined by knative. It is up to debate whether these represent gaps that should be addressed. On the other hand, the scenario mentioned in [2] above presents a possible bug. That being said, I have worked on implementing solutions for all scenarios mentioned above, which are listed below:

1.i. When a knative service is created for an Inference Service or Inference Graph, read the  knative autoscaler configuration defined in the knativeserving custom resource to get the `initial-scale` value. If the requested max replicas is greater than 0 and less than the configured `initial-scale` value, then add the `autoscaling.knative.dev/initial-scale` annotation to the created knative service's template spec with a value equal to the requested max replicas. Alternatively, we can output a log in the kserve-controller-manager pod to inform the user that the globally configured knative initial scale value exceeds the requested max replicas.

1.ii. When a knative service is created for an Inference Service or Inference Graph, by default add the `autoscaling.knative.dev/initial-scale` annotation to the created knative service's template spec with a value equal to the requested min replicas (also solves above.). To prevent limiting the users ability of customizing the initial scale, we can allow users to set the `autoscaling.knative.dev/initial-scale` annotation in the Inference Service or Inference Graph to override the default initial scale functionality. To handle the edge case when 0 initial scale is requested with knative configured to not allow zero initial scale, we can set the initial-scale to 1 since this is the next closest value.

2.i. Always add the `autoscaling.knative.dev/max-scale` annotation to the created knative service's template spec, for **both** Inference Services and Inference Graphs, with a value equal to the requested max replicas.

**References:**
I have a [PR](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/kserve/pull/537) open downstream in opendatahub-io/kserve that implements the changes mentioned in 1.b., specifically for the scenario where 0 min replicas are requested.
[Knative Configuring Scale Bounds Documentation](https://knative.dev/docs/serving/autoscaling/scale-bounds/)
title: Handle Knative Autoscaler Configuration When Creating Knative Services

Current huggingfaceserver requirements [set in pyproject toml](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/huggingfaceserver/pyproject.toml#L15) don't allow the latest version of transformers to be installed as the restriction doesn't allow minor version upgrades.
The latest patch release `v4.42.3` is required in order to run/deploy [gemma2 models](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-2-27b-it).
Current setting in pyproject.toml
```
transformers = "~4.40.2"
```
Which can cause the below issue
```
20.88 The conflict is caused by:
20.88     The user requested transformers==4.42.3
20.88     vllm 0.4.3 depends on transformers>=4.40.0
20.88     outlines 0.0.34 depends on transformers
20.88     huggingfaceserver 0.13.0 depends on transformers<4.41.0 and >=4.40.2
20.88 
20.88 To fix this you could try to:
20.88 1. loosen the range of package versions you've specified
20.88 2. remove package versions to allow pip to attempt to solve the dependency conflict

```

Changing the specification to the below would solve the issue, allowing 4.42.3 to be installed.
```
transformers = "^4.40.2"
```
title: Bump transformers in huggingfaceserver python package

/kind feature

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I would like to request a new feature that allows the `MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH` in the `GRPCServer` class to be configurable. Currently, it is hard-coded to `8388608` (8 MB), which imposes a limitation on the size of image inputs that can be processed via gRPC.  in `kserve/protocol/grpc/server.py`

```python
MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 8388608

class GRPCServer:
    def __init__(self, port: int, data_plane: DataPlane, model_repository_extension: ModelRepositoryExtension):
        self._port = port
        self._data_plane = data_plane
        self._model_repository_extension = model_repository_extension
        self._server = None

    async def start(self, max_workers):
        inference_servicer = InferenceServicer(self._data_plane, self._model_repository_extension)
        self._server = aio.server(
            futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers),
            interceptors=(LoggingInterceptor(),),
            options=[
                ("grpc.max_message_length", MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH),
                ("grpc.max_send_message_length", MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH),
                ("grpc.max_receive_message_length", MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH),
            ],
        )
```
---

The fixed MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH value limits the ability to send larger payloads, such as **high-resolution images**, through gRPC. This restriction can hinder use cases where larger input sizes are necessary for model inference.


I am willing to implement this feature and submit a pull request if approved. Please let me know if this approach aligns with the project’s goals and if there are any specific guidelines I should follow.

I think we need to change `MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH` as configurable through [GRPCServer](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/af54048e126ec302251933bcd260154a75a33b1e/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/grpc/server.py#L32) -> [ModelServer](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/af54048e126ec302251933bcd260154a75a33b1e/python/kserve/kserve/model_server.py#L66) -> [argparse](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/af54048e126ec302251933bcd260154a75a33b1e/python/kserve/kserve/model_server.py#L41) -> ServingRuntime.

Thank you for considering this enhancement.

/kind feature

I would like to add an additional flag to specify a volume to be ReadWrite or ReadOnly.

Currently the implementation for PVC model stores [here](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/pkg/webhook/admission/pod/storage_initializer_injector.go#L255) expects that a PV containing model files is always mounted to a `ServingRuntime` as `ReadOnly`. I have a use case where my server has some internal logic that I would like to dynamically download model components and cache them to the local PV.

As an alternative, this could be a use case for the new model-car, but my download logic is somewhat complex and I need to run the logic in many locations outside of KServe, so keeping the logic inside the container works best for me. **Describe the solution you'd like**
I work on vLLM and I am making a reference architectures that demonstrate best practices for deploying vLLM within KServe. At the moment, I am focused on recommendations for `ModelStorage`.

Given the size of the models (e.g. 70B Llama is 140GB), download time is quite important for autoscaling scenarios. Additionally, in autoscaling scenarios, we often need to scale up to another GPU node, since the model typically uses an entire node (since we need at 4xA100-80GB just to serve the 70B model which will consume all the gpu resources of a node).

As a result, I am trying to design an architecture that enables me to download a model once and then mount the model to each pod as they pop up. 

I really like the OCI user flow (described at https://kserve.github.io/website/0.12/modelserving/storage/oci/), but I was unsure of whether the model assets can be shared across nodes or just within a single node, as it seems like the modelcar container needs to run on a specific node to be accessed by the `InferenceService`:

> As you can see, the Pod has now one additional container. This container is running the modelcar image and runs a ln -s /proc/$$/root/models /mnt/ command to create a symbolic link on a shared empty volume that is mounted on /mnt in the modelcar container and the serving runtime container. The magic here is the symbolic link over proc filesystem, which is shared among all containers. This is possible on Kubernetes for the container's of a Pod if the field .spec.shareProcessNamespace is set to true, which is the case for all storageUri that leverages the oci:// schema.

So, I was wondering:
- Does the OCI image use flow support caching the model weights across nodes?
- If not, is there any plan to expand this OCI image flow to support this?
- If both no, is the best pathway for something like I am describe to use PVCs with `ReadOnly` access method?

To effectively autoscale LLM inference services, we'd like to scale based on metrics like token throughput, power consumption. 

In order to achieve this Autoscaler needs to be able to query metrics from prometheus. KEDA supports [scaling based on prometheus metrics](https://keda.sh/docs/1.4/scalers/prometheus/) and we would like to implement a native integration with KEDA for both serverless and raw deployment mode to support autoscaling LLM inference out of the box.

A few important metrics:
* Time To First Token (TTFT): Low waiting times for a response are essential in real-time interactions, but less important in offline workloads.
* Time Per Output Token (TPOT): Time to generate an output token for each user that is querying our system. This metric corresponds with how each user will perceive the "speed" of the model.
* Latency: The overall time it takes for the model to generate the full response for a user. Overall response latency can be calculated using the previous two metrics: latency = (TTFT) + (TPOT) * (the number of tokens to be generated). 
* Throughput: The number of output tokens per second an inference server can generate across all users and requests. 
* Power consumption: Metrics produced by [Kepler](https://github.com/sustainable-computing-io/kepler), e.g kepler_container_joules_total.


**Anything else you would like to add:**
- Knative has a PoC to integrate with KEDA and @skonto is [creating a new repo](https://github.com/knative/community/issues/1527) for `serving-keda` under knative-extensions org.
- For Raw Deployment mode we can provision the `ScalerObject` in kserve controller and allow user to specify the metrics query on `InferenceService` spec. 

```yaml
apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1"
kind: "InferenceService"
metadata:
  name: "llama2-vllm"
spec:
  predictor:
    scaleQuery: "average_token_throughput_per_second[1m]"
    scaleMetric: custom
    maxReplicas: 10
    minReplicas: 1
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: huggingface
      storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/huggingface/llama2-70b"
```

```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaleObject
metadata:
  name: llama2-vllm-scaleobject
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: llama2-vllm-deployment
  pollingInterval: 15
  cooldownPeriod: 30
  minReplicaCount: 1
  maxReplicaCount: 10
  triggers:
    - type: prometheus
      metadata:
        serverAddress: http://prometheus-server
        metricName: average_token_per_second
        query: average_token_per_second[1m]
        threshold: "500"
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
When configuring custom certificates in both KServe and ModelMesh, the semantics of the `certificate` field differ significantly between the two. In KServe, the certificate field denotes the path to the custom certificate, whereas in ModelMesh, it represents the actual content of the custom certificate.

As a result, when switching between deployment modes (KServe and ModelMesh), conflicts arise. To address this issue, we need to clarify the meaning of certificate in KServe by renaming it to `ca_bundle` ([AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdkref/latest/guide/feature-gen-config.html)), and ensure that both `cabundle_configmap` and `certificate` can coexist in the storage-config to support both controllers.

FYI,
- KServe requires specifying the name of the ConfigMap containing the custom certificate under the `cabundle_configmap` key within the JSON-formatted storage-config Secret to set up custom certificates.

- On the other hand, ModelMesh requires directly inserting the content of the custom certificate into the `certificate` field within the JSON-formatted storage-config Secret to configure custom certificates.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
What we are observing in case of IG router is that even after having graceful shutdown implemented in router there were some 502s observed , while doing re-stacking of pod while it is getting active traffic.  
All of those 502s have been the ones where request entered the container when server has been shutdown. 
**Point to note**: No in-flight requests were impacted that have already been initiated but new requests still came in to the pod.

**Root Cause**:  Now if POD hasn't been de-registered from ingress side but SIGTERM handling has been started in container then no new requests will be served by container but POD will still accept it and will result in 502s.
In essence, there can  be some lag b/w pod getting de-registered from ALB side and pod getting terminated completely.

So, it makes sense to have preStop hook in-place to let pod get de-registered from ingress controller and then trigger graceful Shutdown.

Solution suggested:
Ability to add preStop hook to router's container. One can implement this preStop hook in different ways to make sure POD is no longer receiving traffic and only then SIGTERM is triggered to all the containers in POD.

/kind feature

**Describe the solution you'd like**

In order to support Modelcars as described in this [design document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Bs4fnP8rhPMaoPoLSYVvuRq-z9vkGPQ0rKbmfH4I7js/edit#bookmark=id.qb0sqvo6n1bq), in the PR #3110 and the initial issue #3043 
some additional feature are required from the `ClusterStorageContainer` support.

As described in the design doc:

ClusterStorageContainer as introduced in #3060 allows to flexibly delegate the initialization process to an instance of a custom image that is specified in a custom resource `ClusterStorageContainer`. This feature maps one or more specific URL schemas to a single initialization image that is then used as an init container for a runtime deployment to initialize the model data. This mapping and the image are fixed and provided as part of the KServe installation by the operator persona. A user deploying an `InferenceService` can give the URL prefix but cannot change the image used for it.

The modelcar approach can not directly use the current implementation of the `ClusterStorageContainer` for two reasons:

* A modelcar must be configured as a sidecar, not as an init-container. 
* The user specifies the container image used for a model car as part of the storage URL and cannot be fixed within a `ClusterStorageContainer` upfront.

To integrate modelcars with the ClusterStorageContainer indirection, the following changes might be needed:

* An indication in the `ClusterStorageContainer` CRD that a sidecar container (in `.spec.containers`) should be created instead of an init-container (in `.spec.initContainers`). An enumeration-type field is recommended, something like "setupMode" with values "init-container" (default) and "sidecar" (or "app-container")
* The field `.spec.container.image` would need to be extended to allow a more flexible format to extract the image name from the storage URL provided. A simple way to enable this would be to regexp grouping: The `.spec.supportedUriFormats.regex` could allow capturing groups that could be referred to in the `.spec.container.image` like in this example:

```yaml
apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1"
kind: ClusterStorageContainer
….
spec:
  container:
    # First capturing group from regex matching. Error if no such group exists
    image: "$1"
    …
  supportedUriFormats:
    # Regex with capturing groups
    - regex: "oci://(.+)"
```

* A way for setting the Pod's `.spec.shareProcessNamespace` would be needed. It can't be part of the CSC' `.spec.container` section as this is pod-wide specification (for all containers of the inference service, including the serving runtime specified via the `InferenceService`). Also, being able to set the containers' UID (the one of the sidecar and the one of the main-container with the serving runtime) might be needed in certain circumstances.
   
**Anything else you would like to add:**

Setting up the modelcar container is a bit more involved than setting up init-containers, as it also touches other parts of the overall Pod. The question that we should decide is, whether it makes sense to make the modelcar approach part of the ClusterStorageContainer approach or should stay as an internal handler as implemented in #3110 . The current implementation within the storage initializer is more straightforward, but if the final goal is to move all initialization predefined ClusterStorageContainer, we would need the changes described here.

**Links to the design documents:**

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Bs4fnP8rhPMaoPoLSYVvuRq-z9vkGPQ0rKbmfH4I7js/edit#bookmark=id.qb0sqvo6n1bq
title: Extend ClusterStorageContainer to support Modelcars

**Describe the solution you'd like**
There are some cases where is not desirable to install the `ClusterServingRuntime` CRD, and it is better to only have the namespace-scoped `ServingRuntime`.

The most notable case is in multi-tenant environments, where a single cluster is shared with several teams, users or customers. In such environments, namespaces are given to them and privileges are reduced to that single namespace. Thus, each user/team/customer is expected to create their own `ServingRuntime` in their namespaces.

Clearly, with reduced privileges, users would not be capable of creating `ClusterServingRuntimes`. However, by omitting creation/installation of the `ClusterServingRuntime` in the cluster, the risk of misconfigurations is fully removed.

The solution I would like is simple: provide a configuration flag in helm charts to give the option to omit installation of `ClusterServingRuntime` CRD. Clearly, this would require support in the controller codebase.

body:
/kind feature

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I propose an enhancement for model fetching in KServe using an `oci:` schema for model location. Currently, an init container fetches the model data from a location specified by a URL within the `InferenceService`. This process, however, has several limitations, especially for large models. This proposal aims to reduce startup latency, minimize local disk storage waste, and offer easier optimization methods by fetching the model directly from an OCI image stored in node-local image storage. 

The proposed model setup involves:
1. Adopting an `oci:` URL schema as a reference to the model in an `InferenceService`. 
2. Using a sidecar container, instead of an init-container, added to the Knative Service to hold the actual model. This allows the model to be fully contained and distributed within an OCI image.
3. Configuring the overall Pod as `shareProcessNamespace: true` to ensure all sidecars can access each other's filesystem via `/proc/<pid>/root`. This way, the main container can directly access the model from the data-container.

**Anything else you would like to add:**

This approach could provide several benefits, including:
- Reduced local disk space usage as pods running the same model on a node will access the same directory containing the model.
- Lower startup times due to the elimination of copying potentially large data.
- Ability to leverage known techniques to pre-fetch container images to nodes or use lazy-loading techniques (e.g., with the [stargz snapshotter for containerd](https://github.com/containerd/stargz-snapshotter)).
- Resolution of certain problems encountered with init-containers when using the [init-container with Istio's CNI plugin](https://istio.io/latest/docs/setup/additional-setup/cni/#compatibility-with-application-init-containers).

If the community agrees, I would be keen to work on implementing a Proof of Concept (PoC) to measure the benefits of this approach. I appreciate any feedback and look forward to our discussion.
title: Enhancing KServe Model Fetching with oci: Schema and Sidecar Containers

**Describe the solution you'd like**

In OpenShift, containers are run under a randomly selected user ID. The current images do not play nicely with this; they expect to run with a fixed user id of 1000. I.e., the file access modes cannot deal with this, so the images need to be recreated for OpenShift. See https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/openshift_images/create-images.html for more information about the criteria for running container images on OpenShift.

I.e., from https://docs.openshift.com/container-platform/4.13/openshift_images/create-images.html#use-uid_create-images

>  By default, OpenShift Container Platform runs containers using an arbitrarily assigned user ID. This provides additional security against processes escaping the container due to a container engine vulnerability, thereby achieving escalated permissions on the host node.
> 
> For an image to support running as an arbitrary user, directories and files written to by processes in the image must be owned by the root group and read/writable by that group. Files to be executed must also have group execute permissions.
> 
> Adding the following to your Dockerfile sets the directory and file permissions to allow users in the root group to access them in the built image:

```
RUN chgrp -R 0 /some/directory && \
    chmod -R g=u /some/directory
``` 

> Because the container user is always a member of the root group, the container user can read and write these files.

**Anything else you would like to add:**

Adapting the Dockerfiles accordingly is not harmful and fully compatible with the current usage when the container is running with the UID 1000

body:
/kind feature

## Context
We are working on making `KServe` run on OpenShift. KServe in this case runs on top of OpenShift Serverless (which is basically Knative made running on OpenShift). It is installed based on the updated [guide here](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/docs/OPENSHIFT_GUIDE.md). In this setup we have an additional routing layer in front of the `istio-ingressgateway`. As `Knative` relies on the `Knative Ingress` objects to configure networking we end up with issues in routing. This also applies to alternative `Knative` ingresses like `net-contour`.

## In detail problem description

Examples shortened for brevity. (full yamls available here: https://gist.github.com/ReToCode/40a3da622e039f12fdf778ca1b67a591):

Given the following `InferenceService` 

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: sklearn-iris
  namespace: kserve-demo
status:
  address:
    url: http://sklearn-iris.kserve-demo.svc.cluster.local/v1/models/sklearn-iris:predict
  components:
    predictor:
      address:
        url: http://sklearn-iris-predictor.kserve-demo.svc.cluster.local
      traffic:
      - latestRevision: true
        percent: 100
        revisionName: sklearn-iris-predictor-00001
      url: http://sklearn-iris-predictor-kserve-demo.apps.rlehmann-ocp-4-12.serverless.devcluster.openshift.com
  url: http://sklearn-iris-kserve-demo.apps.rlehmann-ocp-4-12.serverless.devcluster.openshift.com
```

Creates the following `Knative Ingress` :

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.internal.knative.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: sklearn-iris-predictor
  namespace: kserve-demo
spec:
  rules:
  - hosts:
    - sklearn-iris-predictor-kserve-demo.apps.rlehmann-ocp-4-12.serverless.devcluster.openshift.com
    http:
    visibility: ExternalIP
```

**Problem 1**
KServe adds an additional istio `VirtualService` with the domain `sklearn-iris-kserve-demo.apps.rlehmann-ocp-4-12.serverless.devcluster.openshift.com` that `Knative` does not know of. For OpenShift specifically, the issue is that our controller creates OpenShift routes containing the hosts that are defined in `Knative Ingress` objects. So we are missing that additional host, resulting in the url in the `InferenceService` status being not callable.

```yaml
apiVersion: route.openshift.io/v1
kind: Route
metadata:
  name: route-6a86a949-245f-49ea-b081-dfd32e623d62-353934363632
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  host: sklearn-iris-predictor-kserve-demo.apps.rlehmann-ocp-4-12.serverless.devcluster.openshift.com
  port:
    targetPort: https
  tls:
    insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy: Redirect
    termination: passthrough
  to:
    kind: Service
    name: istio-ingressgateway
    weight: 100
  wildcardPolicy: None
status:
  ingress:
    host: sklearn-iris-predictor-kserve-demo.apps.rlehmann-ocp-4-12.serverless.devcluster.openshift.com
```

**Problem 2**
The url in the status field of `InferenceService` does not know/respect that the service is called via `https`. 


### Problem summary
We end up with
- `kubectl get ksvc` returns the domain `https://sklearn-iris-predictor-kserve-demo.apps.rlehmann-ocp-4-12.serverless.devcluster.openshift.com`
- `kubectl get is` returns the domain `http://sklearn-iris-kserve-demo.apps.rlehmann-ocp-4-12.serverless.devcluster.openshift.com`
- The additional host (which is displayed for the user) `sklearn-iris-kserve-demo.apps.rlehmann-ocp-4-12.serverless.devcluster.openshift.com` is not routed by `Knative` or any prevalent routing component like OpenShift router.

## Proposed feature
- Add the ability to configure that external domains are reachable via `https`, even when this happens before `KServe` and `Knative`

## Open points
- I'm not sure how we could fix the wrong "wrapping" service host. How is this intended to work with `kourier` or other ingress Knative solutions? Could we create `Knative Ingress` objects instead of istio specific ones? Have you tried that before? Any other ideas on how to solve this?

/cc @skonto
title: Making the ingress routing more generic

apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1

/kind feature

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Users should be able to define every node as either a hard dependency or a soft dependency in an Inference Graph

**Current situation:**

IG assumes that every node in the graph is a `soft dependency` including the last node.
By `soft dependency`, I mean IG's router doesn't halt IG's execution even if any node returns non-200. It continues executing the graph silently.

For example:
If we have an IG with 3 nodes  => { N1,N2,N3} in a `Sequence`, and now if the middle node, N2, returns non-200, IG will continue to call N3 with N2’s erroneous response body.
So, the user would have to make sure that the N3 node can handle that unexpected and erroneous response body from N2 properly.
Even if N3 (i.e. last node) handles it properly and returns 400 due to bad/unexpected request body, IG will still return 200 since the last node is also a soft dependency. And this behavior is not right.

So, basically IG’s response can not be influenced in any way and is always 200. 

Only exception is, IG will return 500 if something went wrong when IG router called its [node](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/cmd/router/main.go#L53-L63). 
For example: Some http connection error that disrupted the connection.


**Anything else you would like to add:**
To make sure we **do not release a breaking change**, we can rollout this feature keeping every node, including last one, as a soft dependency by default.

Although I feel last should be always a hard dependency. If the last node returns non-200, IG should never return 200. But for the sake of keeping changes non-breaking, we can keep all nodes configurable.

**Initial idea to implement:**
We can add a field in IG spec to mark the node as a `hard` or `soft` dependency to decide whether to stop IG execution right away or not.

- For nodes mentioned as `hard` dependency, IG's execution will stop if that node errors out
- For nodes mentioned as `soft` dependency, IG's execution will not stop and continue
title: Inference Graph’s response code should be influenced by node’s response code

Specifically, the current pain points are:
1. strict equal (==, [boto3](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/release-0.9/python/kserve/requirements.txt#L18)) and tilde equal (~=, [numpy](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/release-0.9/python/kserve/requirements.txt#L12)) do not perform well in terms of backward & forward compatibility, and introduce unnecessary restrictions as a "middle-layer" SDK (downstream customer may have specific reasons to use other versions of boto3/numpy, thus making KServe SDK hard to adopt)
2. Similarly, dependency requirements (even under the >= cases) should ideally be as relaxed as possible, so that customers using some old version of dependencies can still enjoy later version of KServe SDK.
3. Not all dependencies declared as a requirement are actually used by customers, e.g., some customers may not need boto3/azure/google libraries depending on their cloud provider choice; some customers may not need ray[serve] if they are not using parallel inference feature. Such too broad hard dependency pattern can introduce additional risk on adoption, e.g., if one unnecessary dependency can't be installed ([example](https://github.com/ray-project/tune-sklearn/issues/169#issuecomment-1163872731))or introduces conflict in customer env.

Suggestions for dependency management:
1. Use >= instead of ~=/== if possible
2. The dependency version requirement should be as relaxed as possible (e.g. the lower the version number the better) so the python sdk could be more adoptable (give the freedom to pick dependency versions to downstream packages)
3. Introduce optional dependencies ([example](https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/userguide/dependency_management.html#optional-dependencies)) to separate out core functionalities from optional functionalities. Some candidates for optional dependency can be ray and cloud provide specific packages.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
This will solve the issue of transformer redundancy when the first or last node in the InferenceGraph has multiple models (in a splitter or ensemble configuration) using the exact same transformer. 

Consider the example below:

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: sklearn-iris
  namespace: kserve-test
spec:
  transformer:
    containers:
      - image: transformer:1.0
        name: kserve-container
        command:
          - "python"
          - "-m"
          - "custom_transformer.model"
        args:
          - --model_name
          - sklearn-iris
  predictor:
    sklearn:
      storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/sklearn/1.0/model"
---
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: xgboost-iris
  namespace: kserve-test
spec:
  transformer:
    containers:
      - image: transformer:1.0
        name: kserve-container
        command:
          - "python"
          - "-m"
          - "custom_transformer.model"
        args:
          - --model_name
          - xgboost-iris
  predictor:
    xgboost:
      storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/xgboost/iris"
---
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: InferenceGraph
metadata:
  name: ensemble-model
  namespace: kserve-test
spec:
  nodes:
    root:
      routerType: Ensemble
      steps:
        - serviceName: sklearn-iris
          name: sklearn-iris
        - serviceName: xgboost-iris
          name: xgboost-iris
```

Here InferenceGraph has two InferenceServices.  Since same preprocessing is to be done for both these InferenceService objects, same transformer is present in both the InferenceServices. 

When the above configuration is applied, two separate transformer pods will be created. Both the transformer pods will be doing the exact same preprocessing on the same input and hence, there is redundancy here. If I had 10 models above, 10 transformers would be running.

One solution could be to have transformer support at InferenceGraph level. So the above configuration will look like this:

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: sklearn-iris
  namespace: kserve-test
spec:
  predictor:
    sklearn:
      storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/sklearn/1.0/model"
---
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: xgboost-iris
  namespace: kserve-test
spec:
  predictor:
    xgboost:
      storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/xgboost/iris"
---
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: InferenceGraph
metadata:
  name: ensemble-model
  namespace: kserve-test
spec:
  transformer:
    containers:
      - image: transformer:1.0
        name: kserve-container
        command:
          - "python"
          - "-m"
          - "custom_transformer.model"
  nodes:
    root:
      routerType: Ensemble
      steps:
        - serviceName: sklearn-iris
          name: sklearn-iris
        - serviceName: xgboost-iris
          name: xgboost-iris
```

The incoming input would be processed by InferenceGraph's transformer and then would be passed to the models. Having transformer for InferenceGraph will also allow users to process the output of the graph - for eg, it could be used as a reducer model.

**Anything else you would like to add:**
[Miscellaneous information that will assist in solving the issue.]

One alternative solution to the problem would be to allow transformer only InferenceService as requested in #2336 . This would allow for even more possibilities with the InferenceGraph.

Yet another solution may be to allow multiple InferenceService objects to be connected to the same transformer.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
[A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.]

We have a requirement of downloading file from our Hadoop based storage using WebHDFS REST API with TLS (has to provide TLS cert and a header with id). To make it general, TLS and headers can be optional.


User can use the following command to generate the secret:
```sh
kubectl create secret generic hdfscreds \
    --from-file=TLS_CERT=./client.crt \
    --from-file=TLS_KEY=./client.key \
    --from-literal=HDFS_NAMENODE="https://host:port" \
    --from-literal=HDFS_ROOTPATH="/" \
    --from-literal=HEADERS="{'x-my-container': 'my-container'}"
```

format of the secret:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: hdfscreds
type: Opaque
data:
  HDFS_NAMENODE: 'http(s)://host:port'
  HDFS_ROOTPATH: xxxx # string, default: "/"
  TLS_CERT: xxxx # string, default: ""
  TLS_KEY: xxxx # string, default: ""
  TLS_CA: xxxx # string, default: ""
  TLS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY: # string (true|false), default: "false"
  HEADERS: xxxx # string, default: ""
```

To implement it in storage initializer, [hdfscli](https://hdfscli.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart.html#python-bindings) is used.

simple code sample:

```python
from requests import Session
from hdfs.client import Client

HDFS_NAMENODE="https://host:port"
HDFS_ROOTPATH="/"
HEADERS={'x-my-container': 'my-container'} # parse from string
TLS_CERT="path to TLS_CERT"
TLS_KEY="path to TLS_KEY"
TLS_CA="path to TLS_CA"
TLS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY = True|False
FILE_PATH = "path to file or directory"
OUT_PATH = "path to output directory"


s = Session()
s.cert = (TLS_CERT, TLS_KEY)
# s.verify = , True, False, or CA PATH
if TLS_CA:
  s.verify = TLS_CA
if TLS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY:
  s.verify = False

s.headers.update(HEADERS)

# Has to set root to none empty value otherwise it will try to GETHOMEDIRECTORY, but user don't have the permission
client = Client(url=HDFS_NAMENODE, root=HDFS_ROOTPATH, session=s)
status = client.status(FILE_PATH, strict=False)
print(status) # None of not exist

# Downlaod file or directory to output directory
client.download(FILE_PATH, OUT_PATH, n_threads=2)
```

The TLS_CERT and TLS_KEY as well as TLS_CA can be mounted as volume just like GCS or as a temp file if it is supported.


**Anything else you would like to add:**
[Miscellaneous information that will assist in solving the issue.]

https://hadoop.apache.org/docs/stable/hadoop-project-dist/hadoop-hdfs/WebHDFS.html

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Currently, the model type + version support for Serving Runtimes (SR) is not limited to a specific version. For example, a SR with following would support tensorflow models with either version 1 or no version numbers.
    name: tensorflow
    version: "1"
Another SR with following would support tensorflow models with either version 2 or no version numbers.
    name: tensorflow
    version: "2"
When a tensorflow model comes in with no specific version, it could be placed to run on either SR, potentially producing different results.

Suppose a new SR is developed later this year to support only tensorflow 3 (I know not there yet :). Since there is no way to limit a SR to a specific version, an older tensorflow model with no specific version would fail in this SR.

Most of current example models have just model type, no specific versions. So this implied no version support will cause issues later when there are newer SRs for new framework versions.

I would like to suggest to make the SR supported model format more specific. And provide better solution for models with no specific versions. Here are a few potential changes/additions...

1. add "pinToVersion" flag, this alone won't solve the random SR pick issue
2. remove the implied no version support, so the supported model formats are limited to the version in the entry, and if a version is not provided, the SR supports all versions
3. add logic to place a model on the SR that supports the latest framework version when the model has no version and there are multiple SRs supporting the target framework

Would love to get feedback and collectively come up with best solution. Thanks!

Hi everybody! I spent quite some time investigating a configuration issue for the storage-initializer, namely a `STORAGE_URI` env value set like:

```
s3://wmf-ml-models/articlequality/enwiki/20211022183902/model.bin
```
instead of
```
s3://wmf-ml-models/articlequality/enwiki/20211022183902/
```

It was clearly a misconfiguration issue but the log messages from the container made it more confusing:

```
[I 211025 16:39:52 storage-initializer-entrypoint:13] Initializing, args: src_uri [s3://wmf-ml-models/articlequality/enwiki/20211022183902/model.bin] dest_path[ [/mnt/models]

[I 211025 16:39:52 credentials:1102] Found credentials in environment variables.
[I 211025 16:39:52 storage:85] Successfully copied s3://wmf-ml-models/articlequality/enwiki/20211022183902/model.bin to /mnt/models
```
The above seems to suggest that `model.bin` has been copied successfully, meanwhile what happens is that nothing is copied due to the wrong `STORAGE_URI` (that is an object path, rather than something than contains objects).

Same thing if I put a `STORAGE_URI` that points to no objects or to a non-existent path on s3. I believe that the code in https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/kserve/kserve/storage.py#L114 should check if any object is contained in the URI provided, and report an error if nothing is returned (ideally skipping the "Successfully copied ..."). In this way the pod creation would fail at the storage-initializer bootstrap, and not later on (in my case, the kserve-container failed, rightfully, due to the absence of the model.bin file that it was looking for).

) only supports REST call to the predictor, when predictor is using gRPC protocol user has to overwrite the `predict` handler to make the gRPC call with v2 protocol, so we'd like to provide a default implementation similar to the way we did for REST.

1: Add a protocol field on the `InferenceService` [predictor spec](https://github.com/kubeflow/kfserving/blob/master/pkg/apis/serving/v1beta1/predictor.go#L76)

2: We then pass the protocol field to the transformer, so if it is gRPC we can make a async gRPC call with `tritonclient`.
```python
import grpc

def __init__(self, name: str, predictor_host: str):
    channel_options = (("grpc.lb_policy_name", "round_robin"),)
    _channel = grpc.aio.insecure_channel(self.predictor_host, options=channel_options)
    self._client_stub = service_pb2_grpc.GRPCInferenceServiceStub(_channel)

async def predict(self, features: Dict) -> Dict:
    if self.protocol == "gRPC":
        request = _get_inference_request(
            model_name=self.model_name, inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs)
        async_result = await self._client_stub.ModelInfer(
            request=request, timeout=self.predict_timeout)
        response = InferResult(async_result)
```

/kind feature

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Hi!
I'm trying to build a use-case that monitors functional metrics of a model that is deployed with KFServing. In the [samples on github](https://github.com/kubeflow/kfserving/tree/master/docs/samples/metrics-and-monitoring) I discovered there is already some support for technical monitoring using Prometheus, but what we're after here is functional monitoring of model metrics like e.g. feature and prediction distributions. Since I didn't find any documentation on how to do this, I did some investigation on how to make it work as a temporary solution (until the community comes with a unified way to do this). From my own investigation, I found at least three possible ways to go about this:

1. Add some kind of Prometheus  Exporter/Instrumentator to the application server to indicate which metrics should be published on an /metrics endpoint for example, so that they can be scraped by Prometheus. Similar like the simple solution [in this beautiful blog](https://www.jeremyjordan.me/ml-monitoring/) (works with FastAPI).
2. Add a sidecar container that generates input feature and output distribution metrics based on the model's endpoint usage. Similar like [this sidecar agent](https://github.com/MetricRule/metricrule-sidecar-tfserving) that currently does this already with TFServing. AFAU this is a quite clean solution, as it doesn't require changes to your application server.
3. At this very moment I've implemented it in a third way : push the desired metrics to an index in Elastic Search from within the kfserver application server (right before you return the resulting predictions).


My question is if someone is already doing something like this with KFServing, and if the answer is yes, some hints would be really appreciated :blush:. If there are already some plans to bring this functionality to KFServing, I would also be very happy to hear about it.
title: Functional monitoring of a model
